D64 BoozeLoader/ByteBoozer trackmo extraction and decrunching; experimental BASIC/disassembly routines. Inspected repository README and source/tree where relevant.
Curated listings and reference material, without a distinct buildable analysis project.
GitHub fork metadata identifies mist64/final_cartridge parent.
Repository tree contains only an item-list Markdown file.
README index points to separately catalogued game repositories.

Reconstructs v1.20 using Turbo C 2.0 and TASM 1.0. Author reports 96.30% identical load-image bytes after excluding EXE headers/relocations; remaining mismatch includes uninitialized data, so do not mark byte-exact.

Author reports the reconstructed executable is byte-for-byte identical for the documented LZEXE shareware and registered builds. Separate from the same author's modern RigelEngine port; shares historical engine lineage with Cosmore.

Reconstructs v451.03 game C code and most related executables with a functionally equivalent loader. C routines can match original instructions when compiled with Microsoft C 5.1, but executable layout differences and remaining assembly mean no whole-binary exactness claim. Modern port is a separate derivative.

Author reports release builds reproduce original DOS binaries and all three SAR archives bit for bit via build_masm.py --verify; the C/WebAssembly port is playable to the ending. Separate from awkto's independent Zeliard study and SDL port.

Version 1.6 debug symbols informed an author-reported Ghidra/AI decompilation; Borland C++ 3.x build produces PACWARS.EXE, with DOSBox IPX launch scripts. No binary identity or complete gameplay parity established.

The original branch preserves per-function offsets into the v1.1 DOS binary; main has an SDL2 C/C++ port with touch controls and changes. Do not treat the modern executable as a byte-exact DOS reassembly.

Assembly files patch portions of the original DOS executable via incbin; fixes include smooth scrolling, copy-protection bypass, input and sound changes. This is not a full game disassembly or reconstructed source tree.
README documents stripping a 16-bit DOS extender around a 32-bit game and the gog/ tree contains a large rayman_disasm.S listing. Research output is an analysis/disassembly, not a working port.

Partial executable disassembly and tools for RLE, EGA images and castle layouts; extractors recover some volumes and first six castles. Runnable refers to the analysis extractors, not a playable game reconstruction.
Python save decoder/editor and tile decoder derived by modifying and inspecting game data. Author describes map decoding as unfinished and not published; there is no reconstructed gameplay source.

README calls a full Ghidra-derived reimplementation a goal; current UTILS contain music player/converter, resource extractor and graphics format work. Do not report a completed decompilation or playable port.
Viewer/editor for original DAT resources, maps, sprites, images, music, sound, text and triggers. Credits srtuss for the map format and joint research; game executable remains original.

Port of DOS Prince of Persia 1.0 based on the author's separately published IDA disassembly, with later-version features and modern extensions. The Apple II original source is cited as supporting evidence, not the DOS code being catalogued.

Buildable native Carmageddon reimplementation that replaces original assembly with C function by function. Historical Watcom symbols exist but README says they do not match released code positions. Completeness and playable parity remain unverified.

Unofficial modern engine using original game data; README states episode 1 is playable while episodes 2/3, saving and some audio/UI behavior remain incomplete. CPU of original binary not independently established.

From-scratch port of the 1995 DOS shooter; README reports all seven levels and ending playable using original disc image. Documents original programmer's format notes, manual Ghidra analysis, later AI-assisted implementation; modern code is not source-level decompilation.
Primary README explicitly documents 32-bit x86, WebAssembly, ARM Cortex-A7 and TMS320C6745 builds and links Tube64 as its 64-bit successor.

Separate from Duke2Reconstructed: modern C++ engine informed by original DOS disassembly; reads original game data and supports all four episodes. README directs readers to the same author's byte-exact reconstruction for historically faithful DOS code.

Independent repository with SAR/resource tools, original-binary disassembly scripts, documented town/fight systems, SDL port and author-described playthrough. CI tests without game files; parity/playthrough checks need original files. Separate from nolanvenhola's bit-perfect MASM reconstruction.

Earlier independent SCI Companion project corpus with title-specific game.ini, decompiled script source and occasional gameplay fixes; King's Quest I README reports completion testing but a moveButterfly caveat. Overlaps subjects with sluicebox/sci-scripts yet differs in versions, tooling history and human edits; no blanket script-build claim.
Original repository documents a parser, version detection and independent comparison against historical GFA editor output; distinct from tracked gfalist.
Primary README documents distinct reverse-direction format encoder and verification against real GFA-BASIC tools.

Implemented Commodore/NES Ghidra loaders, bundled SNES SPC700/65C816 language variants and bank-aware analysis; current 65C816 work quarantines one named bad oracle vector behind regression tripwires rather than treating it as a language failure.
Reviewed as one coherent multi-system music-sequence archaeology/extraction project; platform directories share one root purpose and do not warrant artificial subproject records.
Tool's README and CLI show concrete CPC-oriented Z80 reverse-engineering capabilities and runnable script.
Cycle-backend game-mod documentation and tests reviewed after the widescreen/mod merge: hooks, isolated calls, save-state records, presented width and custom rendering are opt-in and bounded.
Title-specific README documents native recompilation of verified US ROM and limited playable starting-area functionality.
Primary README documents three distinct game disassembly-to-JavaScript ports and per-frame emulator comparisons within one shared project.

Independent MEGA65/C64 research article on original Crossroads machine-code analysis; links to a renamed Crossroads II disassembly already tracked under MarkRdgOx. Follow original Crossroads research for further substantive artifacts.
Independent Amiga debugger reconstruction using disassembled ARIV/Action Replay material and new features; discovered via broad README search.

Buildable Merlin32/ca65 adaptation of the Brutal Deluxe VisiCalc disassembly. Recovers two regions left undecoded in the earlier listing, corrects code/data boundaries, and generates a DOS 3.3 disk image. README says source-only corrections retain byte-identical binaries; this is credited follow-on analysis, not the original disassembly. Whole-program match against the source binary is not claimed.

Annotated 1983 T&E SOFT ROM assembles to the original verbatim. Enhanced and Enhanced+ variants change graphics, sound, rooms and difficulty; their outputs should not be described as byte-identical to the original. README states the enhanced RAM start is $E000 and its RAM requirement is 8 KB, but does not establish the original ROM's minimum.

Annotated disassembly of Konami's RC727 game. Sjasm can assemble either ROM version using VERSION2; version 2 contains bug fixes. The source file documents the original/version differences; the README does not claim byte-identical builds.

Disassembled BIRDSK2 with WFDis/Beebdis and reassembled it with BeebAsm. Diagnoses and repairs graphical corruption after level 13 and a crash at level 23; includes playable binary, disk image and emulator save states. Later comments incorporate labels from the author's original sources.

Modular Python 3.11+ framework for recovering DOS games and developing native source ports. Combines static facts, original-executable oracle runs, deterministic replays and partial generated or authored implementations; it is a framework, not a completed port of a specific game or a universal decompiler.

Reconstructed C engine for the 1992 DOS English release, with format decoders and documentation. Two Open Watcom targets: structure-faithful BUMPY.EXE is link-only and byte-compared but not run; BUMPYP.EXE adds a host layer and plays in DOSBox with user-supplied game files. Author explicitly describes Claude-led work; no byte-identical final build claim.

Reconstructs the 1993 game from DOS binaries and reports full byte matches for both 1.00 floppy and 1.02 CD-ROM releases. Build recreates a Borland/TASM toolchain and requires user-supplied original game files for play; project also includes a browser-based asset viewer. The author says source cleanup and documentation remain ongoing.

Independent, heavily annotated disassembly of K240's play executable, reassembled with vasm as a drop-in replacement for the original game files. Repairs ship, fleet, economy and UI bugs and credits tetracorp's separate K240 analysis for assistance. The patched output is deliberately different from the original, so no original byte-match is asserted.

Analyzes a user-supplied Amiga WHDLoad install, its BOND-compressed overlays and three partially decoded 68000 modules that reassemble byte-for-byte. A playable Musashi/OCS host still executes original game code; a separate native no-Musashi translation has progressed into live combat but is not a finished whole-game recompilation. Distinct from the tracked Battle Squadron music replayer.

Native C reimplementation of the original Amiga game's gameplay and renderer, using the historical 68000 assembly source as reference and preserving Amiga data formats. SDL2 desktop and Emscripten builds are documented. This is source-derived porting, not a disassembly of an Amiga binary; no Amiga executable is run by the port.

Reverse engineers the packed Stage swaptro extracted from Sanity's Velveteen 18 disk, documents its load address and memory map, and provides buildable 68000 source plus several patch-based visual/music variants. README includes a Makefile workflow for applying patches, assembling and making a floppy; game playability is not applicable to a demo.

Web and Linux workbench for Amiga floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents RDB partition work, Amiga filesystems, resident modules, Hunk analysis, annotated 68k disassembly and exact-hash guarded patches. It is host-side tooling, not software running on an Amiga; some historical-media and emulator-dependent tasks require user-supplied inputs.

Complete, named 68000 source for Reservoir Gods' Atari ST Chu Chu Rocket 1.18 LITE. Default build reproduces CHUCHU.TOS and CHUCHU.LNK byte-identically; optional Reforged optimizations and fixes deliberately differ. README reports tests in Hatari and on a real Mega STe and explicitly credits Claude assistance. This is distinct from the original game's development source.

Builds a new loader, version-guarded patches for the Ator-cracked ST game, a simultaneous third-player mode and a joystick test utility. Fixes TOS 2.06/STE/Mega STE compatibility and requires the user's exact original input file; the game itself is not distributed or built by CI. Patched output is not an original byte-match.

Web and Linux workbench for Atari ST through Falcon floppy, hard-drive, archive and ROM images. Current release documents GEMDOS editing, AHDI/ICD partitions, STX protection reports, flux containers and 68000 analysis. It is host-side tooling, not a native Atari ST application; the Amiga File Forge sibling handles a different platform and formats.

Recovered Tim and Geoff Follin period music and driver source from Tatung Einstein floppies. Author reverse-engineered a 6502 detokenizer and began modern Z80 assembler builds for AY music examples; this is source recovery, not a game disassembly.
Python extraction and documented analysis of original game map, charset, tile and sprite data. Scope is game data; no disassembly or playable reconstruction is claimed.

Disassembled C64 tuning and receiver programs from the 1985 Light Fantastic televised software-transmission experiment and documented receiver behaviour; the author says the recovered receiver appears to lack the storage part.
VICE save states and research notes documenting experimental reverse engineering of C64 demo effects; the README explicitly says the work is still limited in scope.

LangGraph-based research workbench accepts a 64 KB C64 memory dump and question, combines static Capstone disassembly with optional VICE MCP introspection and maintains an evidence-backed knowledge base. Separate from the tracked C64RE/TRX64 projects.
Fully annotated MSX2 Metal Gear disassembly with Sjasm ROM builds for the Japanese and English releases.
Manually annotated Arkanoid MSX disassembly with a documented z80asm rebuild and reference SHA-1.
PC-98 visual-novel engine research, executable disassemblies and format tools covering several engines and games.
Current C++ MES bytecode compiler/decompiler and GP4/GPC/GPA image round-trip tooling for PC-98 visual-novel engines.
Racket predecessor implementation explicitly credited by lime-juice; retained as lineage rather than a duplicate catalogue record.
Long-running bit-perfect source reconstruction of the first five Touhou PC-98 games.

OCR and proofreading restoration of Atari's paper OS-B source listing with a ca65 conversion and ROM comparison checks.
Sparse but substantive annotated 6502 disassembly of Bruce Lee for Atari 8-bit computers.

Redistributed MSX dumping, backup, repair and development tool bundle retained as an ecosystem discovery node.

F# ST emulator boots TOS 1.00 to GEM, runs disk programs and Super Sprint, checks 68000 instruction vectors, and includes ROM/program control-flow investigations.
Port of uae4all-psp to the SF2000/GB300 multicore framework, with ADF loading and working save states; distinct from original UAE and WinUAE.

Atari 2600 emulator with developer debugger, mapper and coprocessor support, and development-focused Supercharger/tape handling.

Consolidated CLI/API for managing annotated 6502 disassemblies across versions, including round-trip verification with BeebAsm; can use Dasmos or py8dis drivers.
Amiga ProTracker 2 continuation based on re-sourcing/disassembly of ProTracker 2.3D; source modifies playback and sample handling, with downloadable executable and bootable ADF.
QBasic Gorillas recreated in C64 BASIC with changed graphics/sound; repository includes authored BASIC source, not a disassembly of the DOS binary.
Instructions for running an older third-party Windows cartridge creator in a VM; no authored cartridge/tool reconstruction in this repository.
CPC/Plus and GX4000 emulator with sub-cycle hardware models, flux-image decoding, an integrated debugger and TCP/headless IPC for scripted analysis; no claim of independent feature verification.

Amstrad CPC firmware adapted to RC2014 with serial keyboard/text I/O and changed firmware routines; compatible BASIC can run through the firmware jump blocks. README describes a temporary pageable-ROM release.

Restored and documented Ian Bell/David Braben original C64 source discs, with BeebAsm build tooling and reference binaries. README shows matching compiled outputs for documented variants; original source provenance is explicit, not a disassembly-derived reconstruction.
KiCad hardware pinout symbols for CPC ICs; no software analysis or developer tool is implemented here.
Arduino-ready Z80 single-instruction disassembler handles incomplete opcode streams; the README explicitly excludes a hardware connection, full-program control-flow analysis and label generation.
Game-specific C64 compatibility engine for recent Covert Bitops titles; assess its execution path and relationship to the games before a catalogue record.
Web/C++ port of the same game-specific engine; assess alongside the Unity implementation rather than counting as a separate game reconstruction.

JavaScript reimplementation derived from CPC DSK and Z80 analysis; documents the original cooperative bytecode VM and includes disasm.c, bytecode listings and assembly. Do not infer byte-exact source.
Hand-redrawn Amiga font assets; the README expressly says the font file format was not reverse engineered.

Portable C recreation of the 1986 ST text-to-speech synthesizer, with original binary disassemblies and documented code-lineage comparison; claims sample-for-sample output, not original source or binary equality.
SNDH/PSG player with 68000 emulation, tracing and reachability-guided SNDH disassembly; output can be edited and reassembled to alter metadata or code.
Amiga device-driver example/template with optional generated objdump output; no legacy-software recovery or standalone analysis tool.

The hardware repository includes authored Amiga RTG driver source under drivers/gfx; README describes reverse-engineering the Picasso96 driver interface to get Workbench running. Scope is the driver, not a claim that the graphics-card hardware is software archaeology.
Action Replay III hardware schematic reproduction, GAL programming files and ROM binaries; no published debugger source reconstruction.
Amiga assembly tutorials and a mixed link list; useful for discovering upstream tools and analyses, not a single recovery project.
VS Code extension integrating VASM/VLINK, FS-UAE/WinUAE run/debug and Capstone disassembly for stack selection and source-less debugging.
Reverse-engineered third-party Amiga HD floppy-drive adapter hardware and PAL logic; no floppy software or media-analysis tool.

Includes ACME-assemblable C64 KERNAL source and release ROMs for C64/1541; README distinguishes the untouched original v1 ROM release. No evidence here of published 1541 source or binary-exact reproduction.

Original MiST Atari ST/STE FPGA core models GLUE/MMU from recovered schematics and shifter from reverse engineering; supports TOS and disk images. MiSTer-devel/AtariST_MiSTer adapts the core to distinct MiSTer board integration.

Board-specific adaptation of gyurco/MiSTery with MiSTer emu top-level, video and peripheral integration. README credits the upstream core, while AtariST.sv names and implements the MiSTer port; distinguish integration work from original chip reverse engineering.
Original CPC BASIC/C homebrew game and sprite-design examples; cited BASIC disassembly is a third-party reference, not project-specific archaeology.
Original browser-based JavaScript compiler and CPC runtime, still receiving bug fixes. README points to CPCBasicTS as a separately maintained TypeScript continuation with new features.
TypeScript continuation based on benchmarko/CPCBasic 0.9.20, with independently developed features including tokenized BASIC and DSK/ZIP import; the original JavaScript codebase has its own record.
Python tools list visible/hidden ROM commands, dump strings with optional XOR decoding and patch Graduate CP/M accessory ROM personal data; analysis is tied to real CPC ROM structures.
Cross-development collection includes AMSDOS header viewer, DSK sector tooling, screenshot/media converters and Caprice 32-derived emulator; README describes unfinished components separately.

The Documentation/VDP Emulator directory supplies original/patched Vampire Killer Z80 listings and diffs explaining Aleste game BIOS/VDP adaptation; surrounding repository is a broader Aleste hardware/software archive. Build and current playability not established.

Original Angus Duggan source discs, documented and modernized for BeebAsm; README compares built outputs with reference binaries and reports matching released variants, without calling this a disassembly.

Restored and documented Ian Bell/David Braben source discs for BBC Micro with 6502 Second Processor, with variant builds and reference-binary checksum checks; original source, not binary-derived disassembly.
Mixed archive of period CPC sources, tools and commercial work; components need individual attribution and scope before promotion.
Go emulator with Spectrum/CPC/MSX/NES and arcade modes, debugger/breakpoint flags and tests. README labels systems as incomplete (e.g. CPC 80%), so do not imply complete fidelity.
Authored Python scripts edit the Jose Leandro 512K cartridge ROM menu and insert game ROMs at known offsets; author disclaims authorship of original ROM and cartridge.
Port of the author’s new game to AmigaOS using offline sprite baking; no historical-game binary research or reusable analysis tool.
Native port of available OpenTTD 1.0.5 source to AmigaOS with substantial new platform drivers; no recovery of historical binaries established.

Original PRG self-extractor executed with Py65; recovered C64 code, graphics and timing informed a native Z80 Spectrum 48K TAP. RE notes explicitly reject cycle-perfect equality and document changed display and controls.; Separate JavaScript/canvas reimplementation of this repository’s native Spectrum port. README explicitly says there is no Z80 emulator or embedded binary and explains timing differences; do not equate it with a C64 direct port.
Original Z80 breadboard computer tutorial and schematics; no legacy-software reconstruction or separate analysis tool.
Replacement CPC keyboard PCB designs and matrix wiring; hardware only.
Hypothetical new 6502 CPC-like computer based on inspiration from a prototype PCB, not a reconstruction of its software.
CPC-compatible modular hardware and small test ROM/assembly snippets; no separately implemented CPC software archaeology project.
Untested HAL/PAL replacement hardware design and behavior tests; no developer software or recovered firmware.
Early work-in-progress Pascal-like cross compiler targeting Z80, with compiler, emulator and IDE source; README does not establish production use.
Hyperlinked CPC firmware manual, useful to verify firmware/jumpblock semantics but not an implemented analysis tool.
Original Z80 LCD circuit and test code; hardware tutorial outside legacy software/tooling scope.
Reusable 50 Hz scrolling engine and developer tools, sprite cache/multiplexer, loaders and example disk/cartridge builds; not a reconstruction of Steel Ranger or MW ULTRA.
Author website and downloadable C64 tool/game archive; useful as a provenance source, not an independent single software project.
Original C64 game source; retain to audit the specific games actually run by OldschoolEngine 2, not a binary reconstruction.
Original low-raster-time C64 music player with GoatTracker 2 converter and source; v2 is separately maintained and changes effects and hard restart behavior.
New player implementation retains lineage with cadaver/miniplayer but adds ADSR/waveform commands and changes hard restart and memory layout; README documents speed and NTSC tradeoffs.
Original Metal Warrior 4 C64 game source, useful context for the author’s game-specific emulator lineage.
Emulates 6502 instructions to dump SID register activity; README version history documents illegal opcode, multispeed and CPU-cycle profiling support.
Configurable recursive SID file scanner matches wildcard/skip-byte patterns against playroutine signatures; identifies provenance candidates rather than proving authorship.
Original source of the C64 Steel Ranger demo; useful for the OldschoolEngine 2 audit, not itself reverse engineering.
Acorn Electron binary-only consumer CHIP-8 emulator without documented developer debugger, analysis or source recovery capabilities.

Original developers captured a Spectrum snapshot, profiled executed regions and produced editable Z80 assembly; README says intro and second stage are absent and source is not yet ready for complete reassembly. CPC release is historical context only.

Authored browser game logic and scenes using assets from the CPC version and explicitly crediting Giner/Pazos disassembly/SDL work; README calls it playable with known bugs. Distinct Web implementation, not an independently recovered CPC disassembly.
VS Code C64 development suite with toolchain, resource compilers, VICE debugging, embedded 6502 emulation and disassembly; Atari ST search origin was incidental.

Retargetable assembler that also generates a disassembler and examples/tests from instruction definitions; README marks many architectures partial and explicitly supports usable 6502 and Game Boy programs.
Translates C64 BASIC and KERNAL behavior from documented disassemblies to the DCPU-16 fantasy CPU, with working command subset and PETSCII/display adaptation; not an original 6502 source archive.
Adapts the 1984 C64 SMON monitor to a Ben Eater style 6502 machine with serial IO and HEX loading; published assembly and ROM, with explicit removed C64 disk/printer features.
Traces 6502 code into IR and emits .NET MSIL for execution, with C64 and NES example emulators; JIT handles self-modifying code via invalidation. Distinct from highbyte/dotnet-6502 system emulator.
Annotated assembly adapts BBC BASIC to a Ben Eater-style 6502 ROM with serial I/O. Credits annotated BBC BASIC ROM disassemblies; README calls it alpha and warns LCD/keyboard drivers are broken.
Historical Windows/OS/2 Kermit terminal and file-transfer application source; this candidate documents an application continuation without a specific recovery or retro development tool contribution.
MAME front end with a custom Apple II/Macintosh-focused MAME build and Uthernet II support; a system emulator rather than a disassembly.
Maintained Jaguar and Jaguar CD libretro emulator. Repository documents processor/peripheral models and hardware-behavior test suite; no claim of new reverse engineering of a particular game.
General file-system-independent archive/recovery container; no historical computer software or platform-specific analysis in the project scope.
Curated website of retro reverse-engineering articles, file formats and source/code links. Retain as a discovery source for targeted follow-up, not as one project for every outbound link.
Beta reimplementation of WarpOS powerpc.library API/ABI for PowerPC PCI accelerators on Amiga. The repository is described as a CVS mirror; preserve that provenance.
Amiga-specific ISO C runtime and headers written from scratch to support GCC-based Amiga development. No claim that it was recovered from a binary.
HID to Amiga/Atari input adapter hardware and firmware; no independent historical-software recovery or developer-analysis tool evidenced.
GPL AmiTCP/IP 3.0b2 fork with separately implemented Roadshow-compatible bsdsocket.library extensions based on the published SDK ABI. Explicitly does not contain or disassemble Roadshow code.

Python MCP server and AmigaOS C daemon for remote shell, files, screenshots, ARexx and GUI interaction. README states AmigaOS 2.04 and bare 68000 for agent; AI integration is described, not an assertion about code authorship.
Full GEOS KERNAL 2.0 disassembly, reorganized and optimized for customization. README documents ACME/make assembly; altered sources are not asserted byte-identical to the original.
Game engine reimplementation based on reversing the original Windows executable; original Bermuda Syndrome game data is required.
Fade to Black engine reimplementation that loads original PC retail/demo data. README lists rendering and game options; original files are required.
Yaga-engine wrapper for two Humongous Entertainment games, using original .exe and .he/.da2 data. README flags missing lipsync; assess exact reverse-engineering lineage separately.
Disassembles NES ROM and rewrites hardware I/O to 65C816 routines before assembling a SNES ROM. Indirect jump targets require runtime observation and manual inclusion; compatibility is limited.
Open silicon pin-compatible Z80 CPU replacement with tapeout and PCB validation; hardware recreation outside the software catalogue.
Research and reproducible cycle/memory comparisons of more than 120 credited 6502 multiplication routines; useful developer reference, not a game disassembly.
Distinct Basilisk II libretro port for SF2000/GB300, emulating classic Macintosh and requiring a ROM and HFS disk image. No special debugging capability claimed.
